newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India awards term diesel and kerosene tenders.
newsitem.headline: India awards term diesel and kerosene tenders.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp has awarded Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), BB Energy, Glencore and Marubeni a one-year term tender to supply a total of 3.2 million tonnes of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and 540,000 tonnes of 0.25 percent sulphur diesel, traders said on Monday.

At the same time, India has awarded a one-year term buying tender to supply 30,000 tonnes per month of superior kerosene to KPC for delivery to the west coast at $1.32 per barrel above spot MidEast quotes on a cost-and-freight basis (c-and-f).
The IOC also cancelled its spot buying tender for June superior kerosene.
The term tenders for diesel and kerosene cover deliveries from June 1997 to May 1998.

Traders said the awarded volume of 1.0-percent diesel was higher than had been expected. They said in the currently running term tender, India receives three cargoes per month of 45,000 tonnes each and they had expected a similar award.
But the latest award for 1.0-percent diesel is for four cargoes of 45,000 tonnes each and one cargo of 87,000 tonnes per month.
Traders said KPC was awarded two 45,000 tonne cargoes per month of 1.0-percent diesel at 30 cents per barrel over MidEast quotes fob Kuwait.
Marubeni was awarded the 87,000-tonne monthly cargo at 91 cents per barrel c-and-f west coast.
BB Energy and Glencore were awarded one 45,000-tonne monthly cargoes, each at $2.04 premium to MidEast quotes c-and-f.
The 0.25-percent 45,000-tonne diesel cargo per month was awarded to KPC at $2.14 per barrel over MidEast quotes delivered to the west coast.
